Thematic analysis remains the dominant qualitative method in UX research teams, but researchers are increasingly pairing it with AI-assisted coding. Several teams report using GPT-4 to pre-code transcripts before human review.

The adoption of LLMs in research workflows has accelerated in 2025. Many practitioners now use AI-assisted tools for interview transcription and initial thematic coding. However, the say-do gap between stated and actual AI adoption in research teams remains significant.

Dovetail released a major update to its analysis features, now supporting automated theme clustering. UserTesting also announced deeper Figma integration for prototype testing. These tooling changes are reshaping how unmoderated usability sessions are run.

Research ops functions are struggling with the democratization of research. As more product managers conduct their own surveys and usability tests, professional UX researchers report concerns about methodological quality and the risk of confirmation bias.

A preprint on arXiv by researchers from CHI 2026 suggests that synthetic participants generated by LLMs can approximate some — but not all — behavioral patterns of real users. The study recommends using synthetic data for hypothesis generation, not validation.

Behavioral shifts around AI trust are emerging as a major research theme. Longitudinal studies show that user trust in AI-generated recommendations erodes faster than trust in human recommendations after a single bad experience.

The UX research job market contracted in late 2024, with several large tech companies reducing research headcount. This has increased interest in research automation tools and prompted debate about the long-term ROI of embedded vs. centralized research teams.

Grounded theory approaches are seeing renewed interest in product research contexts, particularly for studying emerging behaviors around AI product usage where existing frameworks fall short.

Cognitive walkthrough and heuristic evaluation methods are being adapted for conversational AI interfaces. Traditional Nielsen heuristics do not map cleanly to LLM-powered products, prompting methodological innovation.

Survey-based research is facing validity challenges. Straight-lining and speeders remain persistent problems in online panels, while response rates for B2B surveys have dropped to historic lows.

A new paper in CSCW explores how participatory design methods can be applied to AI system development, arguing that contextual inquiry with end users should precede any model fine-tuning.

Mental model shifts around subscription pricing are significant in the consumer fintech space. Diary study data suggests users now default to skepticism about auto-renewing services, representing a behavioral change from pre-2022 baselines.

The CHI 2026 conference saw a notable uptick in papers on mixed methods approaches combining log data analysis with qualitative interview studies. Several papers proposed new frameworks for quant-qual integration.

Research infrastructure investment is growing at companies with high research maturity. Evidence chains linking research insights to product decisions are becoming a key metric for demonstrating research impact to leadership.
